CLIPORA / GUIDE

How to clear the clipboard on Windows

The current clipboard, Windows + V history and an app’s saved library are different places. Clear the one that contains the information you want to remove.

Reviewed 29 October 2026 · Clipora editorial

On this page
Replace the current clipboardDelete Windows clipboard historyClear Clipora’s separate libraryWhat clearing cannot promise

Replace the current clipboard

Copy harmless text, such as “clipboard cleared”, to replace the item you would paste with Ctrl + V. This does not erase earlier items already saved in Windows history, Clipora or another application.

Clipora also has a Clear current clipboard tray action. Use it when you want to empty the current clipboard rather than copy replacement text.

Delete Windows clipboard history

  1. Press Windows + V.
  2. Use an item’s menu to delete that item, or choose Clear all.
  3. Review pinned items separately: Clear all keeps pins. Unpin and delete any you want removed.

You can also use Settings → System → Clipboard → Clear clipboard data. Microsoft describes this as clearing data on the device and in its cloud clipboard, except pinned items. The exact controls depend on your Windows version and account.

Clear Clipora’s separate library

In Clipora, use a clip’s … → Delete action, then review the confirmation. To stop future recording while you work with sensitive information, choose Pause. Automatic retention and clearing unpinned history protect pins; an explicit confirmed deletion can remove a pin.

Unpinning alone does not delete a clip. Closing the library window does not stop recording: Clipora stays in the tray. Choose Pause or Quit when appropriate.

What clearing cannot promise

Deleting an entry is not a secure disk wipe. Previously exported backups, other apps’ histories and copies already pasted into documents can still contain the text. Review those separately.

For future copies, configure application exclusions and pause before copying passwords, tokens or private records. Not every application marks its clipboard data as sensitive.

Windows instructions: Microsoft’s clipboard guide. Reviewed 29 October 2026. Labels can vary with your Windows build.
